props.full_label: Small business smash and grab spree, Eastside and Snohomish County, 2018
props.area: Kirkland, Sammamish, Redmond, Bothell, Issaquah, Lynnwood, Mill Creek, Everett, Monroe, WA
props.outcome: One defendant was arrested 5 Oct 2018 and charged that week with four burglary counts, one attempted burglary, trafficking in stolen property and methamphetamine possession, with bail of 225,000 dollars. The second defendant was arrested 8 Sep 2018 on 19 felony counts. Later outcome not found.

props.notes: Only the month is given, as early June, and the time is described as night. Three businesses on one row of storefronts were struck: an insurance agent, an Indian restaurant and a cafe. The fingerprint match is to a Seattle man, and police in King County knew his name as early as 6 Jul. The Herald article does not say which of the two defendants committed each incident.

evidence.description: Glass smashed at the storefronts
A fingerprint on an office drawer came back as an apparent match to the Seattle man

props.notes: Only the month is given, as early July. Vietnamese restaurant. The thief cut himself while breaking in. DNA swabs from blood on a table leg later matched the Seattle man, per charges filed in October. The Herald article does not say which of the two defendants committed each incident.

evidence.description: Blood on a table leg; DNA swabs later matched the Seattle man

props.notes: A business near Silver Lake. The man was caught moments after the break-in, early on 14 Jul, sitting in a stolen van at a nearby gas station. A baggie in his backpack tested positive for methamphetamine. Snohomish County prosecutors charged him with three counts of burglary after this arrest. The Herald article does not say which of the two defendants committed each incident.

evidence.description: Window punching tool on the front seat of the van
Suspect was sitting in a stolen van at a nearby gas station moments after the break-in
Broken glass found in the suspect's shoe

props.notes: A storage facility and a sewing and vacuum business, kept together as one record. The suspect was arrested three blocks away. The Herald article does not say which of the two defendants committed each incident.
